  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# proto-migrate
2	
3	Versioned message codec for records written by older releases: readers decode any known version and migrate it forward to the current shape.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m proto_migrate --selftest
16	
17	## Online, resumable log migration
18	
19	`migrate-log` migrates an append-only JSONL log (mixed v1/v2/v3
20	records, one object per line) to the current version **while other
21	processes keep appending to it**.  Appenders never have to stop or wait
22	for a silent window: every concurrently appended record is migrated in
23	its original order, with zero loss and zero duplication.  The pass is
24	streaming and never loads the file into memory:
25	
26	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-log app.log            # strict (default)
27	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-log app.log --skip
28	
29	Python entry point:
30	
31	```python
32	from proto_migrate import migrate_log_file, read_log
33	
34	result = migrate_log_file("app.log", on_bad="strict")  # or on_bad="skip"
35	# result.records_migrated / records_skipped / records_salvaged / replaced
36	# result.post_commit_error is a warning string, never a failure
37	
38	records = read_log("app.log")   # one consistent view during a migration
39	```
40	
41	Options: `--strict` (default) / `--skip` choose bad-record handling;
42	`--segment-size BYTES` (default 16 MiB) rotates the temp segments;
43	`--quiesce-ms MS` (default 50 ms) is how long EOF must hold before the
44	input is considered complete while appenders may still be writing.
45	
46	### Checkpoints and resume
47	
48	Migrated output is first written to fsynced, size-bounded segment files
49	in `<file>.migrate-tmp/`.  Every completed segment is covered by a
50	durable record in `<file>.migrate-tmp/checkpoint` containing the input
51	offset already consumed, the migrated and skipped record counts, the
52	cumulative "needs rewrite" flag, and the segment's durable size (the
53	record is fsynced together with its directory).
54	
55	If the process is killed at *any* point, rerunning the same command
56	continues from the newest valid checkpoint: already migrated bytes are
57	neither rescanned nor rewritten, and the finished file is byte-for-byte
58	identical to one uninterrupted run.  Before trusting a checkpoint the
59	rerun validates it and **rolls back to the previous complete
60	checkpoint** when it finds:
61	
62	- a corrupt checkpoint file or a torn half-line at its end;
63	- a referenced segment that is missing or shorter than recorded;
64	- a source-inode mismatch (an earlier run already committed) or a
65	  different `--strict/--skip` policy (strict must re-examine lines a
66	  prior skip run passed).
67	
68	Rollback truncates the checkpoint log to its good prefix, truncates
69	retained segments to their recorded sizes, and deletes unknown
70	segments; the affected input range is then migrated again.
71	
72	### Atomic commit and error classification
73	
74	After the scan and a final quiesced drain, a commit marker
75	(`<file>.committed`) is published and fsynced, then the assembled file
76	is atomically `os.replace`d over the original followed by a directory
77	fsync.  **The atomic rename is the single success/failure border:**
78	
79	- a failure before the rename (I/O error, or a bad record in strict
80	  mode) leaves the original file and every completed segment intact;
81	- a durability or cleanup failure *after* the rename (directory fsync,
82	  commit marker, temp cleanup) never turns the already-committed
83	  migration into a failure: the run exits `0` and the fault is reported
84	  on stderr as a `warning:` (and in `MigrationResult.post_commit_error`).
85	
86	Exit codes: `0` success (including post-commit durability warnings),
87	`1` I/O error, `2` usage error, `3` bad record in strict mode.
88	
89	### Concurrent readers and appenders
90	
91	- **Readers**: use `read_log(path)`, which returns one complete,
92	  version-consistent snapshot — either the whole pre-migration content
93	  decoded as stored, or the whole post-migration content normalized to
94	  the current version.  Old and new field shapes never mix inside one
95	  view, not even when a writer reopens the path by name and appends
96	  during the migrator's wrap-up (the commit marker gates the switch and
97	  every snapshot pins one inode; a record caught mid-append, without a
98	  terminating newline, is excluded).  Opening the path directly gets
99	  the same atomic guarantee at the rename itself (`os.replace`); a
100	  descriptor opened before the rename keeps reading the old inode.
101	- **Appenders must write whole records in one `O_APPEND` write.**
102	  Records appended during the scan are drained into the output.  After
103	  the commit, a convergence phase drains writers that still hold the old
104	  descriptor (via the unlinked old inode) and rewrites old-format
105	  records a path-reopening writer landed on the new inode via further
106	  atomic replacements.  Every repair rebuilds the post-base suffix in
107	  rename-generation order, so a record whose single whole-record write
108	  straddles a rename still lands in its original position.  Convergence
109	  finishes only after two consecutive fully quiet rounds (the last
110	  operations are reads, never a rename); a writer that appends
111	  continuously past the hard backstop (`max(5 s, quiesce*200)`) is not
112	  blocked on forever — rerun the command, it is idempotent and catches
113	  up.  The unavoidable boundary is a writer preempted *between* opening
114	  the path and issuing its one write for longer than convergence runs:
115	  that record reaches an unlinked inode no path-based tool can see, so
116	  the append must be one prompt whole-record write (the stated
117	  contract).
118	
119	### Bad records
120	
121	Corrupt lines, JSON parse failures, missing/non-integer/unsupported `v`,
122	illegal fields, and `NaN`/`Infinity` amounts (including numeric
123	literals such as `1e999` that overflow to infinity) are bad records.
124	An amount of `-0.0` is preserved verbatim.
125	
126	- `--strict`: stop at the first bad line, exit with code **3**, and
127	  leave the original file untouched.
128	- `--skip`: skip bad lines, keep migrating, and write one audit entry
129	  per skipped line to **stderr** as `<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>`.
130	
131	### Idempotency
132	
133	If every record is already at the current version in the canonical
134	encoding and there is nothing to skip, the file is left byte-for-byte
135	untouched (no rename, no mtime change). A second run rewrites no bytes,
136	and a run that recovered from a crash finishes byte-identical to a run
137	that was never interrupted.
138	
139	## Group migration: `migrate-logs`
140	
141	`migrate-logs` migrates a whole **group** of log files in one shot.
142	The group is indivisible: either every member ends up at the current
143	version or every member stays exactly as it was — no partially
144	migrated group is ever left behind after a handled failure or a kill.
145	The member list is always given explicitly, and each member may be
146	appended to by a *different* process while the migration runs:
147	
148	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-logs a.log b.log c.log          # strict
149	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-logs a.log b.log c.log --skip
150	
151	Python entry points:
152	
153	```python
154	from proto_migrate import migrate_log_group, read_log_group
155	
156	result = migrate_log_group(["a.log", "b.log"], on_bad="strict")  # or "skip"
157	# result.records_migrated / records_skipped / records_salvaged / replaced
158	# result.members is a tuple of per-member MigrationResult
159	# result.post_commit_error is a warning string, never a failure
160	
161	records = read_log_group(["a.log", "b.log"])  # one consistent group snapshot
162	```
163	
164	The member list must be a non-empty sequence without duplicate paths
165	(a single path string is not a sequence); a non-sequence raises
166	`TypeError`, an empty or duplicated list raises `ValueError` (CLI exit
167	`2`).  A member that is missing or unreadable raises
168	`FileNotFoundError` at both entry points (CLI exit `1`).
169	
170	### Group work files and the commit marker
171	
172	Group metadata lives next to the **first** listed member:
173	
174	- `.migrate-logs.lock` (sibling of the first member) — the group lock;
175	- `.migrate-logs-tmp/` — the group work directory, holding
176	  `manifest.json` (the member list plus the bad-record policy) and the
177	  **group commit marker `group-committed`**;
178	- `<file>.migrate-group-tmp/` — one directory per member (a sibling of
179	  that member, so every rename stays within one directory and one
180	  filesystem), holding that member's segmented output, its local
181	  `checkpoint`, the assembled `final`, and the `prepared` marker;
182	- `<file>.migrate-group-staged` and `<file>.migrate-group-backup` —
183	  short-lived staging/backup names used by the rename protocol;
184	- `<file>.committed` — the same per-file commit marker the single-file
185	  entry publishes before its rename.
186	
187	**Purpose of the commit marker.** `group-committed` is the single
188	success/failure border of the group.  It is created (temp file +
189	atomic rename + directory fsync) only after *every* member's rename
190	has landed and before any original is deleted.  A rerun checks it
191	first: marker missing ⇒ the whole group is rolled back to the
192	originals and the migration is retried; marker present ⇒ every member
193	is completed forward (never rolled back).  The per-file
194	`<file>.committed` marker gates `read_log`/`read_log_group`, so a
195	reader can never open a post-rename inode under the pre-commit policy;
196	like the single-file entry it is intentionally **kept** after a
197	successful run so readers keep getting normalized views even when a
198	writer later reopens the path and appends old-format records (an
199	idempotent rerun rewrites those bytes).
200	
201	**Cleanup timing.** After the group marker is published, the run
202	converges racing appenders per member, deletes each
203	`<file>.migrate-group-backup`, and finally removes the group work
204	directory `.migrate-logs-tmp/` (taking `group-committed`, the manifest
205	and member temp state with it) and the per-member
206	`<file>.migrate-group-tmp/` directories.  If that cleanup fails, or
207	the process is killed first, nothing is lost: the marker survives, the
208	next run finishes forward and sweeps the leftovers.  Any such
209	durability/cleanup failure after the border is reported on stderr as a
210	`warning:` (and in `post_commit_error`); the run still exits `0`.  The
211	lock files are empty, reusable, and left in place like the
212	single-file lock.
213	
214	### Cross-file two-phase rename and rollback
215	
216	Each member whose bytes change goes through the recoverable sequence
217	`final → <file>.migrate-group-staged`, publish `<file>.committed`,
218	`<file> → <file>.migrate-group-backup`,
219	`<file>.migrate-group-staged → <file>` (each step directory-fsynced).
220	Only once all members have completed this sequence is
221	`group-committed` published.  A kill mid-sequence is resolved
222	deterministically on the rerun from whichever of `staged`/`backup`/the
223	live path survive: without the group marker every member is put back
224	byte-for-byte as it was; with it the remaining renames are completed.

227	
228	Each member writes the same fsynced segments and local checkpoint as a
229	single-file run.  Once a member reaches the group commit phase it
230	records `prepared`; on rerun it is neither rescanned nor rewritten —
231	its `final` is reused — so an interrupted group finishes
232	byte-for-byte identical to one uninterrupted run.  A member failure
233	*before* the group border (including the first bad line in strict
234	mode) rolls every prepared member back: no member's original file is
235	modified and no partial intermediate is left in durable state.
236	
237	### Group snapshots and bad records
238	
239	`read_log_group([...])` reads the whole group in one call and returns a
240	flat record list (members in list order, lines in file order) with no
241	old/new field mix between or within members — including while a
242	path-reopening appender writes old records during wrap-up.  While the
243	entire group is still pre-commit and entirely old-format, records are
244	returned exactly as stored (v1/v2); as soon as any member has crossed
245	its border, every member is normalized to the current version in
246	memory, which is exactly the eventual committed content.
247	
248	Bad-record rules are unchanged.  In strict mode the **first bad line of
249	the whole group** (members in list order) raises `ValueError` and aborts
250	before any rename; exit code is `3`.  In skip mode migration continues
251	and each skipped record is written to **stderr** as
252	
253	    <filename>:<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>
254	
255	Missing/non-integer/unsupported `v`, wrong field types, and `NaN`,
256	`Infinity` or values overflowing to infinity (e.g. `1e999`) are bad
257	records; `-0.0` is preserved verbatim.  The summary counters count
258	only records the invocation newly migrates; an idempotent finish reports
259	`migrated=0`.

261	## Linked migration with cross-group references: `migrate-linked-logs`
262	
263	`migrate-linked-logs` migrates **several groups** of log files whose
264	records reference each other across groups — for example detail records
265	whose `order_id` names an order record in the orders group.  All groups
266	and all references migrate as one unit: either every group ends at the
267	current version with every reference resolving to an existing, complete
268	target record, or every group stays exactly as it was.  Each member may
269	still be appended to by a different process while the migration runs:
270	
271	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-linked-logs \
272	        --group orders.log --group details.log \
273	        --link 1:0:order_id:order_id                # strict (default)
274	    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-linked-logs \
275	        --group orders.log --group details.log \
276	        --link 1:0:order_id:order_id --skip
277

279	`--link SRC:DST:SRC_FIELD:DST_FIELD` declares that a record of group
280	`SRC` whose string field `SRC_FIELD` equals `k` references the record
281	of group `DST` whose `DST_FIELD` is `k` (repeatable; group indices
282	follow the `--group` order).

284	Python entry points:
285	
286	```python
287	from proto_migrate import migrate_linked_logs, read_linked_logs
288	
289	result = migrate_linked_logs(
290	    [["orders.log"], ["details.log"]],
291	    links=[(1, 0, "order_id", "order_id")],
292	    on_bad="strict",            # or "skip"
293	)
294	# result.records_migrated / records_skipped / references_bad
295	# result.records_salvaged / replaced / members / post_commit_error
296	
297	snapshot = read_linked_logs([["orders.log"], ["details.log"]])
298	# one flat record list per group, version-consistent across all groups
299	```
300	
301	The group list must be a non-empty sequence of non-empty member
302	sequences with no path repeated anywhere (a bare path string is not a
303	sequence): a non-sequence raises `TypeError`, an empty or duplicated
304	list raises `ValueError` (CLI exit `2`).  A member that is missing or
305	unreadable raises `FileNotFoundError` at both entry points (CLI exit
306	`1`).

308	### Bad references
309	
310	Four classes of bad references are recognised: **dangling** (no live
311	record in the target group has the referenced key), **target skipped**
312	(the key belongs to a line skipped as a bad record, or to a record
313	dropped over its own bad references), **cyclic** (the reference sits on
314	a record-level reference cycle), and **illegal target version** (the
315	key belongs to a line whose version key is missing, non-integer or
316	unsupported).

318	- `--strict`: the first bad line *or* bad reference of the whole run
319	  (groups in list order, members in list order, lines in file order)
320	  raises `LinkedBadReferenceError` / `GroupBadRecordError` (both
321	  `ValueError`) before any rename; every original stays untouched, exit
322	  code `3`.
323	- `--skip`: bad lines are skipped with the usual audit entry, and
324	  records holding bad references are dropped from the migrated output;
325	  each dropped record is audited to **stderr** as
326	  `<filename>:<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>`.  The summary counts bad
327	  records (`skipped`) and bad references (`refs_bad`) separately, and
328	  both counters only cover records this invocation newly migrates and
329	  references it newly resolves.
330	
331	Migration output uses the unchanged encoding, field defaults and drop
332	rules; the `-0.0` / non-finite amount semantics are exactly the
333	single-file ones.
334	
335	### Durability, resume and snapshots
336	
337	Every member is prepared with the same fsynced segments and durable
338	checkpoints as a single-group run, plus a durable per-line index
339	classifying every consumed source line.  Reference resolution is
340	streaming with bounded memory: keys and edges live in an SQLite spill
341	file inside the group work directory (`.migrate-linked-tmp/` next to
342	the first group's first member), never loading a whole group into
343	memory.  The group commit marker `linked-committed` is the single
344	success/failure border — published only after every member's rename
345	landed — and a kill at any point reruns deterministically: without the
346	marker every member is rolled back byte-for-byte (prepared members
347	resume from their checkpoints and line indexes without rescanning),
348	with it the remaining renames are completed forward.  The result is
349	byte-for-byte identical to one uninterrupted run, and durability or
350	cleanup failures after the marker are warnings (exit `0`), never
351	failures.
352	
353	`read_linked_logs` returns one consistent snapshot of all groups in a
354	single call: old and new field shapes never mix between groups, between
355	members or inside a member — including while a path-reopening appender
356	writes old-format records during wrap-up.
357	
358	## Tests
359	
360	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
361	
362	The migration tests cover three-way concurrency (migrator + appender +
363	reader), resume from checkpoints, checkpoint corruption / missing
364	segment / torn-tail rollback, real `SIGKILL` crash injection and
365	recovery, post-commit fault classification, and idempotent reruns.
366	
367	## Public interface
368	
369	`proto_migrate.dumps(message) -> bytes` encodes the current version.
370	- `proto_migrate.loads(data) -> dict` decodes any known version.
371	- `proto_migrate.migrate(message, target_version) -> dict` converts a decoded message.
372	- `proto_migrate.migrate_log_file(path, ...) -> MigrationResult` runs the online, resumable in-place log migration.
373	- `proto_migrate.read_log(path) -> list[dict]` returns one version-consistent snapshot of a migrating log.
374	- `proto_migrate.migrate_log_group(paths, ...) -> GroupMigrationResult` migrates an explicit group of logs as one all-or-nothing unit.
375	- `proto_migrate.read_log_group(paths) -> list[dict]` returns one version-consistent snapshot of a whole group.

380	
381	## Tests
382	
383	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

386	
387	Values must be JSON-compatible scalars, lists and objects.

# proto-migrate

Versioned message codec for records written by older releases: readers decode any known version and migrate it forward to the current shape.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m proto_migrate --selftest

## Online, resumable log migration

`migrate-log` migrates an append-only JSONL log (mixed v1/v2/v3
records, one object per line) to the current version **while other
processes keep appending to it**.  Appenders never have to stop or wait
for a silent window: every concurrently appended record is migrated in
its original order, with zero loss and zero duplication.  The pass is
streaming and never loads the file into memory:

    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-log app.log            # strict (default)
    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-log app.log --skip

Python entry point:

```python
from proto_migrate import migrate_log_file, read_log

result = migrate_log_file("app.log", on_bad="strict")  # or on_bad="skip"
# result.records_migrated / records_skipped / records_salvaged / replaced
# result.post_commit_error is a warning string, never a failure

records = read_log("app.log")   # one consistent view during a migration
```

Options: `--strict` (default) / `--skip` choose bad-record handling;
`--segment-size BYTES` (default 16 MiB) rotates the temp segments;
`--quiesce-ms MS` (default 50 ms) is how long EOF must hold before the
input is considered complete while appenders may still be writing.

### Checkpoints and resume

Migrated output is first written to fsynced, size-bounded segment files
in `<file>.migrate-tmp/`.  Every completed segment is covered by a
durable record in `<file>.migrate-tmp/checkpoint` containing the input
offset already consumed, the migrated and skipped record counts, the
cumulative "needs rewrite" flag, and the segment's durable size (the
record is fsynced together with its directory).

If the process is killed at *any* point, rerunning the same command
continues from the newest valid checkpoint: already migrated bytes are
neither rescanned nor rewritten, and the finished file is byte-for-byte
identical to one uninterrupted run.  Before trusting a checkpoint the
rerun validates it and **rolls back to the previous complete
checkpoint** when it finds:

- a corrupt checkpoint file or a torn half-line at its end;
- a referenced segment that is missing or shorter than recorded;
- a source-inode mismatch (an earlier run already committed) or a
  different `--strict/--skip` policy (strict must re-examine lines a
  prior skip run passed).

Rollback truncates the checkpoint log to its good prefix, truncates
retained segments to their recorded sizes, and deletes unknown
segments; the affected input range is then migrated again.

### Atomic commit and error classification

After the scan and a final quiesced drain, a commit marker
(`<file>.committed`) is published and fsynced, then the assembled file
is atomically `os.replace`d over the original followed by a directory
fsync.  **The atomic rename is the single success/failure border:**

- a failure before the rename (I/O error, or a bad record in strict
  mode) leaves the original file and every completed segment intact;
- a durability or cleanup failure *after* the rename (directory fsync,
  commit marker, temp cleanup) never turns the already-committed
  migration into a failure: the run exits `0` and the fault is reported
  on stderr as a `warning:` (and in `MigrationResult.post_commit_error`).

Exit codes: `0` success (including post-commit durability warnings),
`1` I/O error, `2` usage error, `3` bad record in strict mode.

### Concurrent readers and appenders

- **Readers**: use `read_log(path)`, which returns one complete,
  version-consistent snapshot — either the whole pre-migration content
  decoded as stored, or the whole post-migration content normalized to
  the current version.  Old and new field shapes never mix inside one
  view, not even when a writer reopens the path by name and appends
  during the migrator's wrap-up (the commit marker gates the switch and
  every snapshot pins one inode; a record caught mid-append, without a
  terminating newline, is excluded).  Opening the path directly gets
  the same atomic guarantee at the rename itself (`os.replace`); a
  descriptor opened before the rename keeps reading the old inode.
- **Appenders must write whole records in one `O_APPEND` write.**
  Records appended during the scan are drained into the output.  After
  the commit, a convergence phase drains writers that still hold the old
  descriptor (via the unlinked old inode) and rewrites old-format
  records a path-reopening writer landed on the new inode via further
  atomic replacements.  Every repair rebuilds the post-base suffix in
  rename-generation order, so a record whose single whole-record write
  straddles a rename still lands in its original position.  Convergence
  finishes only after two consecutive fully quiet rounds (the last
  operations are reads, never a rename); a writer that appends
  continuously past the hard backstop (`max(5 s, quiesce*200)`) is not
  blocked on forever — rerun the command, it is idempotent and catches
  up.  The unavoidable boundary is a writer preempted *between* opening
  the path and issuing its one write for longer than convergence runs:
  that record reaches an unlinked inode no path-based tool can see, so
  the append must be one prompt whole-record write (the stated
  contract).

### Bad records

Corrupt lines, JSON parse failures, missing/non-integer/unsupported `v`,
illegal fields, and `NaN`/`Infinity` amounts (including numeric
literals such as `1e999` that overflow to infinity) are bad records.
An amount of `-0.0` is preserved verbatim.

- `--strict`: stop at the first bad line, exit with code **3**, and
  leave the original file untouched.
- `--skip`: skip bad lines, keep migrating, and write one audit entry
  per skipped line to **stderr** as `<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>`.

### Idempotency

If every record is already at the current version in the canonical
encoding and there is nothing to skip, the file is left byte-for-byte
untouched (no rename, no mtime change). A second run rewrites no bytes,
and a run that recovered from a crash finishes byte-identical to a run
that was never interrupted.

## Group migration: `migrate-logs`

`migrate-logs` migrates a whole **group** of log files in one shot.
The group is indivisible: either every member ends up at the current
version or every member stays exactly as it was — no partially
migrated group is ever left behind after a handled failure or a kill.
The member list is always given explicitly, and each member may be
appended to by a *different* process while the migration runs:

    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-logs a.log b.log c.log          # strict
    python3 -m proto_migrate migrate-logs a.log b.log c.log --skip

Python entry points:

```python
from proto_migrate import migrate_log_group, read_log_group

result = migrate_log_group(["a.log", "b.log"], on_bad="strict")  # or "skip"
# result.records_migrated / records_skipped / records_salvaged / replaced
# result.members is a tuple of per-member MigrationResult
# result.post_commit_error is a warning string, never a failure

records = read_log_group(["a.log", "b.log"])  # one consistent group snapshot
```

The member list must be a non-empty sequence without duplicate paths
(a single path string is not a sequence); a non-sequence raises
`TypeError`, an empty or duplicated list raises `ValueError` (CLI exit
`2`).  A member that is missing or unreadable raises
`FileNotFoundError` at both entry points (CLI exit `1`).

### Group work files and the commit marker

Group metadata lives next to the **first** listed member:

- `.migrate-logs.lock` (sibling of the first member) — the group lock;
- `.migrate-logs-tmp/` — the group work directory, holding
  `manifest.json` (the member list plus the bad-record policy) and the
  **group commit marker `group-committed`**;
- `<file>.migrate-group-tmp/` — one directory per member (a sibling of
  that member, so every rename stays within one directory and one
  filesystem), holding that member's segmented output, its local
  `checkpoint`, the assembled `final`, and the `prepared` marker;
- `<file>.migrate-group-staged` and `<file>.migrate-group-backup` —
  short-lived staging/backup names used by the rename protocol;
- `<file>.committed` — the same per-file commit marker the single-file
  entry publishes before its rename.

**Purpose of the commit marker.** `group-committed` is the single
success/failure border of the group.  It is created (temp file +
atomic rename + directory fsync) only after *every* member's rename
has landed and before any original is deleted.  A rerun checks it
first: marker missing ⇒ the whole group is rolled back to the
originals and the migration is retried; marker present ⇒ every member
is completed forward (never rolled back).  The per-file
`<file>.committed` marker gates `read_log`/`read_log_group`, so a
reader can never open a post-rename inode under the pre-commit policy;
like the single-file entry it is intentionally **kept** after a
successful run so readers keep getting normalized views even when a
writer later reopens the path and appends old-format records (an
idempotent rerun rewrites those bytes).

**Cleanup timing.** After the group marker is published, the run
converges racing appenders per member, deletes each
`<file>.migrate-group-backup`, and finally removes the group work
directory `.migrate-logs-tmp/` (taking `group-committed`, the manifest
and member temp state with it) and the per-member
`<file>.migrate-group-tmp/` directories.  If that cleanup fails, or
the process is killed first, nothing is lost: the marker survives, the
next run finishes forward and sweeps the leftovers.  Any such
durability/cleanup failure after the border is reported on stderr as a
`warning:` (and in `post_commit_error`); the run still exits `0`.  The
lock files are empty, reusable, and left in place like the
single-file lock.

### Cross-file two-phase rename and rollback

Each member whose bytes change goes through the recoverable sequence
`final → <file>.migrate-group-staged`, publish `<file>.committed`,
`<file> → <file>.migrate-group-backup`,
`<file>.migrate-group-staged → <file>` (each step directory-fsynced).
Only once all members have completed this sequence is
`group-committed` published.  A kill mid-sequence is resolved
deterministically on the rerun from whichever of `staged`/`backup`/the
live path survive: without the group marker every member is put back
byte-for-byte as it was; with it the remaining renames are completed.

    <filename>:<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>

records; `-0.0` is preserved verbatim.  The summary counters count

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

13	Encoding is a compact JSON object plus a trailing newline: "v" first,
14	then the fields in that version's field order, with no whitespace
15	inside the object.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import json
21	import math
22	from collections.abc import Mapping
23	
24	__all__ = [
25	    "VERSIONS",
26	    "CURRENT_VERSION",
27	    "dumps",
28	    "loads",
29	    "migrate",
30	    "migrate_log_file",
31	    "read_log",
32	    "migrate_log_group",
33	    "read_log_group",
34	    "migrate_linked_logs",
35	    "read_linked_logs",
36	    "BadRecordError",
37	    "GroupBadRecordError",
38	    "LinkedBadReferenceError",
39	    "GroupMigrationResult",
40	    "LinkedMigrationResult",
41	    "MigrationResult",
42	    "run_cli",
43	    "run_group_cli",
44	    "run_linked_cli",
45	]
46	
47	VERSIONS = (1, 2, 3)
48	CURRENT_VERSION = 3
49	
50	_FIELDS = {
51	    1: ("order_id", "amount", "tags"),
52	    2: ("order_id", "amount", "tags", "status"),
53	    3: ("order_id", "amount", "status", "note", "updated_at"),
54	}
55	
56	
57	def _is_int(value):
58	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)
59	
60	
61	def _is_amount(value):
62	    return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool)
63	
64	
65	def _is_tags(value):
66	    return isinstance(value, list) and all(isinstance(item, str) for item in value)
67	
68	
69	_CHECKERS = {
70	    "order_id": lambda v: isinstance(v, str),
71	    "amount": _is_amount,
72	    "tags": _is_tags,
73	    "status": lambda v: isinstance(v, str),
74	    "note": lambda v: isinstance(v, str),
75	    "updated_at": _is_int,
76	}
77	
78	
79	def _default(name):
80	    if name == "status":
81	        return "new"
82	    if name == "note":
83	        return ""
84	    if name == "updated_at":
85	        return 0
86	    if name == "tags":
87	        return []
88	    raise ValueError(f"no default for field {name!r}")
89	
90	
91	def _validate_fields(message, version):
92	    for name in _FIELDS[version]:
93	        if name not in message:
94	            raise ValueError(f"missing field {name!r} for version {version}")
95	        if not _CHECKERS[name](message[name]):
96	            raise ValueError(
97	                f"field {name!r} has wrong type for version {version}"
98	            )
99	    amount = message["amount"]
100	    if isinstance(amount, float) and (math.isnan(amount) or math.isinf(amount)):
101	        raise ValueError("amount must be a finite number")
102	
103	
104	def _check_version(version):
105	    if not _is_int(version):
106	        raise ValueError("version key 'v' must be an integer")
107	    if version not in _FIELDS:
108	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported version: {version!r}")
109	
110	
111	def dumps(message):
112	    """Encode a field mapping (without "v") as the current version."""
113	    if not isinstance(message, Mapping):
114	        raise ValueError("message must be a mapping")
115	    if "v" in message:
116	        raise ValueError("message must not contain 'v'")
117	    _validate_fields(message, CURRENT_VERSION)
118	    payload = {"v": CURRENT_VERSION}
119	    for name in _FIELDS[CURRENT_VERSION]:
120	        payload[name] = message[name]
121	    text = json.dumps(
122	        payload,
123	        ensure_ascii=True,
124	        separators=(",", ":"),
125	        allow_nan=False,
126	    )
127	    return (text + "\n").encode("utf-8")
128	
129	
130	def _reject_constant(value):
131	    raise ValueError(f"non-JSON constant: {value}")
132	
133	
134	def loads(data):
135	    """Decode bytes of any known version into a mapping including "v"."""
136	    if not isinstance(data, bytes):
137	        raise TypeError("loads expects bytes")
138	    try:
139	        obj = json.loads(data.decode("utf-8"), parse_constant=_reject_constant)
140	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
141	        raise ValueError("invalid JSON payload") from exc
142	    if not isinstance(obj, dict):
143	        raise ValueError("payload must be a JSON object")
144	    if "v" not in obj:
145	        raise ValueError("payload is missing version key 'v'")
146	    _check_version(obj["v"])
147	    version = obj["v"]
148	    _validate_fields(obj, version)
149	    result = {"v": version}
150	    for name in _FIELDS[version]:
151	        result[name] = obj[name]
152	    return result
153	
154	
155	def migrate(message, target_version):
156	    """Convert a decoded message to the target version's shape."""
157	    if not isinstance(message, Mapping):
158	        raise TypeError("message must be a mapping")
159	    if "v" not in message:
160	        raise TypeError("message is missing version key 'v'")
161	    if not _is_int(target_version) or target_version not in _FIELDS:
162	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported target version: {target_version!r}")
163	    _check_version(message["v"])
164	    result = {"v": target_version}
165	    for name in _FIELDS[target_version]:
166	        if name in message:
167	            result[name] = message[name]
168	        else:
169	            result[name] = _default(name)
170	    return result
171

1	"""Cross-group, reference-integrity migration of linked JSONL log groups.
2	
3	This builds on :mod:`proto_migrate.group_migration` (one all-or-nothing
4	group of logs) and adds *references between groups*: records of one
5	group name a record of another group by a key field -- for example a
6	detail record whose ``order_id`` points at an order record in the
7	orders group.  :func:`migrate_linked_logs` migrates every group to the
8	current record version **and** enforces referential integrity in one
9	atomic unit: either every group is migrated with every reference
10	resolving to an existing, complete target record, or every group stays
11	exactly as it was.
12	
13	Link declarations
14	-----------------
15	References are declared by the caller; nothing is guessed from file
16	contents.  ``links`` is a sequence of
17	``(src_group, dst_group, src_field, dst_field)`` tuples: a record in
18	group ``src_group`` whose string field ``src_field`` has value ``k``
19	*references* the record(s) of group ``dst_group`` whose string field
20	``dst_field`` equals ``k``.  Group indices refer to the ``groups``
21	argument order.  A record with several declared source fields carries
22	one reference per field; a non-string field value is not a reference.
23	
24	Bad references
25	--------------
26	Four classes of bad references are recognised:
27	
28	  1. **dangling** -- no live record in the target group has the
29	     referenced key;
30	  2. **target skipped** -- the referenced key belongs to a line that
31	     was skipped as a bad record (or to a record dropped because its
32	     own references are bad);
33	  3. **cyclic** -- the reference sits on a record-level reference
34	     cycle (a record on a cycle has all of its outgoing references
35	     rejected);
36	  4. **illegal target version** -- the referenced key belongs to a
37	     line whose version key is missing, non-integer or unsupported.
38	
39	In ``"strict"`` mode the first bad line *or* bad reference of the whole
40	run (groups in list order, members in list order, lines in file order)
41	raises :class:`LinkedBadReferenceError` / :class:`GroupBadRecordError`
42	(both :class:`ValueError`) before any rename, leaving every original
43	untouched.  In ``"skip"`` mode bad lines are skipped exactly as in the
44	single-group migration and records holding bad references are dropped
45	from the migrated output; each dropped record is audited to the audit
46	stream as ``<filename>:<lineno>:<first 32 raw bytes>``.  The summary
47	counts bad records (``records_skipped``) and bad references
48	(``references_bad``) separately, and both counters only cover records
49	this invocation newly migrated and references it newly resolved.
50	
51	Durability, resume and snapshots
52	--------------------------------
53	Every member is prepared with the same segmented temp output and
54	durable checkpoints as a single-group run, plus a durable per-line
55	index (``lines`` in the member work directory) classifying every
56	consumed source line.  Reference resolution is streaming: keys and
57	edges live in an SQLite spill file inside the group work directory, so
58	no group is ever loaded into memory wholesale.  A killed run resumes
59	prepared members from their checkpoints and line indexes without
60	rescanning them, rebuilds the reference index from those durable
61	indexes, and finishes byte-for-byte identical to one uninterrupted
62	run.  The group commit marker ``linked-committed`` is the single
63	success/failure border; durability or cleanup failures after it are
64	warnings (exit 0), never failures.
65	
66	:func:`read_linked_logs` returns one version-consistent snapshot of
67	every group in a single call -- old and new field shapes never mix
68	between groups, between members or inside a member, including while a
69	path-reopening appender writes old records during wrap-up.
70	"""
71	
72	from __future__ import annotations
73	
74	import argparse
75	import fcntl
76	import json
77	import os
78	import shutil
79	import sqlite3
80	import struct
81	import sys
82	from collections.abc import Sequence
83	from typing import NamedTuple
84	
85	from . import CURRENT_VERSION, migrate
86	from .log_migration import (
87	    DEFAULT_QUIESCE,
88	    DEFAULT_SEGMENT_SIZE,
89	    EXIT_BAD_RECORD,
90	    EXIT_ERROR,
91	    EXIT_OK,
92	    EXIT_USAGE,
93	    LINE_BAD_VERSION,
94	    LINE_GOOD,
95	    BadRecordError,
96	    MigrationResult,
97	    _audit_line,

101	)

103	    _AuditPrefix,
104	    _acquire_member_locks,
105	    _prepare_member,

107	    _publish_member_marker,
108	    _read_checkpoint_log,

113	    "LinkedBadReferenceError",
114	    "LinkedMigrationResult",
115	    "migrate_linked_logs",
116	    "read_linked_logs",
117	    "run_linked_cli",
118	]
119	
120	_LINKED_DIR_NAME = ".migrate-linked-tmp"
121	_LINKED_LOCK_NAME = ".migrate-linked.lock"
122	_LINKED_COMMITTED = "linked-committed"
123	_LINKED_COMMITTED_TMP = "linked-committed.tmp"

126	_LINKED_FINAL = "linked-final"

135	# Mirrors log_migration._FAULT_ENV; post-border cleanup faults injected

137	_FAULT_ENV = "PROTO_MIGRATE_FAULT_AT"

141	_REASON_BAD_VERSION = 3

143	_REASON_CYCLE = 5

145	_REASON_TEXT = {

147	    _REASON_TARGET_SKIPPED: "reference target was skipped as a bad record",
148	    _REASON_BAD_VERSION: "reference target has an illegal version key",

157	class LinkedBadReferenceError(ValueError):
158	    """Strict-mode bad reference, annotated with the source position."""
159	
160	    def __init__(self, path, lineno, raw, cause):
161	        self.path = path

168	class LinkedMigrationResult(NamedTuple):
169	    groups: tuple

171	    records_skipped: int
172	    references_bad: int
173	    records_salvaged: int

179	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
180	# Validation
181	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
182	
183	
184	def _normalize_groups(groups):
185	    """Validate the caller-given list of member lists.
186	
187	    A non-sequence (including a single path string) is a TypeError; an
188	    empty group list, an empty group, or a path repeated anywhere
189	    across the groups is a ValueError.
190	    """
191	    if isinstance(groups, (str, bytes, os.PathLike)) or not isinstance(
192	        groups, Sequence
193	    ):
194	        raise TypeError("groups must be a sequence of member sequences")
195	    out = []
196	    seen = set()
197	    for group in groups:
198	        if isinstance(group, (str, bytes, os.PathLike)) or not isinstance(
199	            group, Sequence
200	        ):
201	            raise TypeError("each group must be a sequence of members")
202	        members = []
203	        for item in group:
204	            path = os.fspath(item)
205	            if isinstance(path, bytes):
206	                path = os.fsdecode(path)
207	            absolute = os.path.abspath(path)
208	            if absolute in seen:
209	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate member path: {path!r}")
210	            seen.add(absolute)
211	            members.append(path)
212	        if not members:
213	            raise ValueError("group member list is empty")
214	        out.append(members)
215	    if not out:
216	        raise ValueError("group list is empty")
217	    return out
218	
219	
220	def _normalize_links(links, group_count):
221	    """Validate link declarations; return a list of 4-tuples."""
222	    if links is None:
223	        return []
224	    if isinstance(links, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(links, Sequence):
225	        raise TypeError(
226	            "links must be a sequence of "
227	            "(src_group, dst_group, src_field, dst_field)"
228	        )
229	    out = []
230	    seen = set()
231	    for link in links:
232	        if isinstance(link, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(
233	            link, Sequence
234	        ) or len(link) != 4:
235	            raise ValueError(f"malformed link declaration: {link!r}")
236	        src_g, dst_g, src_field, dst_field = link
237	        for index in (src_g, dst_g):
238	            if not isinstance(index, int) or isinstance(index, bool) \
239	                    or not 0 <= index < group_count:
240	                raise ValueError(
241	                    f"link group index out of range: {link!r}"
242	                )
243	        for field in (src_field, dst_field):
244	            if not isinstance(field, str) or not field:
245	                raise ValueError(
246	                    f"link field must be a non-empty string: {link!r}"
247	                )
248	        key = (src_g, dst_g, src_field, dst_field)
249	        if key in seen:
250	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate link declaration: {link!r}")
251	        seen.add(key)
252	        out.append(key)
253	    return out

255	
256	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
257	# Work-directory layout
258	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
259

263	    return os.path.join(first_dir, _LINKED_DIR_NAME)

271	    marker = path + ".committed"
272	    return {
273	        "staged": path + _STAGED_SUFFIX,
274	        "backup": path + _BACKUP_SUFFIX,
275	        "marker": marker,
276	        "marker_tmp": marker + ".tmp",
277	    }

340	# Rename debris reconciliation (crash recovery)
341	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
342	
343	
344	def _reconcile_linked_member(path, committed):
345	    """Resolve one member's interrupted rename state, deterministically."""
346	    d = _linked_debris(path)
347	    parent = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
348	    staged = os.path.exists(d["staged"])
349	    backup = os.path.exists(d["backup"])
350	    live = os.path.exists(path)
351	    touched = staged or backup
352	
353	    if committed:
354	        if staged and live and not backup:
355	            os.replace(path, d["backup"])
356	            os.replace(d["staged"], path)
357	            _fsync_dir(parent)
358	        elif staged and backup and not live:
359	            os.replace(d["staged"], path)
360	            _fsync_dir(parent)
361	        _remove(d["marker_tmp"])
362	        _fsync_dir(parent)
363	        return
364	
365	    if staged and backup and not live:
366	        os.replace(d["backup"], path)
367	        _fsync_dir(parent)
368	        _remove(d["staged"])
369	    elif staged and live and not backup:
370	        _remove(d["staged"])
371	    elif backup and live and not staged:
372	        os.replace(path, d["staged"])
373	        os.replace(d["backup"], path)
374	        _fsync_dir(parent)
375	        _remove(d["staged"])
376	    elif backup and not live and not staged:
377	        os.replace(d["backup"], path)
378	        _fsync_dir(parent)
379	    if touched:
380	        _remove(d["marker_tmp"])
381	        _fsync_dir(parent)
382	
383	
384	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
385	# Per-member durable line index
386	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
387	
388	
389	class _LineIndex:
390	    """Durable map of every source line a member's prepare consumed.
391	
392	    One variable-length record per consumed line: a ``<qBBI`` header
393	    (source offset, kind, reserved, projection length) followed by the
394	    projection -- a JSON object of the link-involved string fields of
395	    the *migrated* record (or, for a skipped line, of a lenient parse
396	    of the raw line).  The index is fsynced before every checkpoint
397	    record, so a trusted checkpoint never covers unindexed lines.
398	    """
399	
400	    def __init__(self, member_dir, fields):
401	        self._path = os.path.join(member_dir, _LINES_NAME)
402	        self._fields = tuple(sorted(fields))
403	        self._fh = None
404	
405	    def begin(self, total_lines, resumed):
406	        """Open the index; on resume truncate it to the checkpoint prefix."""
407	        if resumed and os.path.exists(self._path):
408	            keep = self._prefix_bytes(total_lines)
409	            with open(self._path, "r+b") as f:
410	                f.truncate(keep)
411	                f.flush()
412	                os.fsync(f.fileno())
413	            self._fh = open(self._path, "ab")
414	        else:
415	            # Fresh start -- or the index vanished while checkpoints
416	            # survived; the caller's post-prepare consistency check
417	            # detects the mismatch and restarts the member.
418	            self._fh = open(self._path, "wb")
419	
420	    def _prefix_bytes(self, total):
421	        count = 0
422	        pos = 0
423	        try:
424	            f = open(self._path, "rb")
425	        except OSError:
426	            return 0
427	        with f:
428	            while count < total:
429	                header = f.read(_LINE_HEADER.size)
430	                if len(header) < _LINE_HEADER.size:
431	                    break
432	                _off, _kind, _reserved, plen = _LINE_HEADER.unpack(header)
433	                f.seek(plen, os.SEEK_CUR)
434	                pos = f.tell()
435	                count += 1
436	        return pos
437	
438	    def record(self, offset, kind, payload):
439	        proj = self._project(kind, payload)
440	        blob = json.dumps(
441	            proj, ensure_ascii=True, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True
442	        ).encode("ascii")
443	        self._fh.write(_LINE_HEADER.pack(offset, kind, 0, len(blob)))
444	        self._fh.write(blob)
445	
446	    def _project(self, kind, payload):
447	        if not self._fields:
448	            return {}
449	        try:
450	            if kind == LINE_GOOD:
451	                # The migrated, canonical output bytes.
452	                obj = json.loads(payload)
453	            else:
454	                # A skipped bad line: parse leniently (NaN/Infinity
455	                # tolerated) so its key fields still identify it as a
456	                # reference target.
457	                obj = json.loads(
458	                    payload.decode("utf-8"),
459	                    parse_constant=lambda _c: None,
460	                )
461	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
462	            return {}
463	        if not isinstance(obj, dict):
464	            return {}
465	        return {
466	            f: obj[f] for f in self._fields
467	            if isinstance(obj.get(f), str)
468	        }
469	
470	    def sync(self):
471	        self._fh.flush()
472	        os.fsync(self._fh.fileno())
473	
474	    def close(self):
475	        if self._fh is not None:
476	            try:
477	                self._fh.close()
478	            finally:
479	                self._fh = None

482	def _stream_line_entries(member_dir):
483	    """Yield ``(lineno0, offset, kind, projection)`` in source line order."""
484	    path = os.path.join(member_dir, _LINES_NAME)
485	    with open(path, "rb") as f:
486	        lineno0 = 0
487	        while True:
488	            header = f.read(_LINE_HEADER.size)
489	            if len(header) < _LINE_HEADER.size:
490	                return
491	            offset, kind, _reserved, plen = _LINE_HEADER.unpack(header)
492	            blob = f.read(plen)
493	            if len(blob) < plen:
494	                return
495	            proj = json.loads(blob) if plen else {}
496	            yield lineno0, offset, kind, proj
497	            lineno0 += 1
498	
499	
500	def _count_line_entries(member_dir):
501	    try:
502	        return sum(1 for _ in _stream_line_entries(member_dir))
503	    except OSError:
504	        return -1

512	class _LinkedMember:
513	    def __init__(self, index, group_index, path, member_dir, src, dirty,
514	                 offset, lineno, run_migrated, run_skipped, fresh_from):
515	        self.index = index
516	        self.group_index = group_index
517	        self.path = path
518	        self.member_dir = member_dir
519	        self.src = src
520	        self.dirty = dirty
521	        self.offset = offset
522	        self.lineno = lineno
523	        # Records this invocation newly migrates; salvaged is added
524	        # after the border.  Lines before ``fresh_from`` were migrated
525	        # by an earlier (killed) run and are not counted again.
526	        self.run_migrated = run_migrated
527	        self.run_skipped = run_skipped

533	def _prepare_linked_member(index, group_index, path, member_dir, on_bad,
534	                           segment_size, quiesce, audit_stream, fields):
535	    """Prepare one member with its durable line index."""
536	    member = _prepare_member(
537	        path, member_dir, on_bad, segment_size, quiesce,
538	        _AuditPrefix(audit_stream, path),
539	        line_index=_LineIndex(member_dir, fields),
540	    )
541	    if _count_line_entries(member_dir) != member.lineno:
542	        # The line index and the checkpoints disagree (e.g. the index
543	        # file was lost between runs): restart the member from scratch
544	        # so both are rebuilt consistently.
545	        try:
546	            member.src.close()
547	        except OSError:
548	            pass
549	        shutil.rmtree(member_dir, ignore_errors=True)
550	        member = _prepare_member(
551	            path, member_dir, on_bad, segment_size, quiesce,
552	            _AuditPrefix(audit_stream, path),
553	            line_index=_LineIndex(member_dir, fields),
554	        )
555	    _write_linked_prepared(member_dir, {
556	        "dirty": member.dirty, "offset": member.offset,
557	        "lineno": member.lineno,
558	    })
559	    fresh_from = member.lineno - (member.run_migrated + member.run_skipped)
560	    return _LinkedMember(
561	        index, group_index, path, member_dir, member.src, member.dirty,
562	        member.offset, member.lineno, member.run_migrated,
563	        member.run_skipped, fresh_from,
564	    )

567	def _resume_linked_prepared(index, group_index, path, member_dir, on_bad):
568	    """Fast path: a member fully prepared before the kill is not redone."""
569	    info = _read_linked_prepared(member_dir)
570	    if info is None:
571	        return None
572	    inode, mode, _records, _good = _read_checkpoint_log(member_dir)
573	    try:
574	        current_inode = os.stat(path).st_ino
575	    except OSError:
576	        return None
577	    if inode != current_inode or mode != on_bad:
578	        return None
579	    if _count_line_entries(member_dir) != int(info["lineno"]):
580	        # The line index no longer matches the checkpointed line count:
581	        # restart this member from scratch (its checkpoints are
582	        # discarded with the work directory).
583	        shutil.rmtree(member_dir, ignore_errors=True)
584	        return None
585	    if info["dirty"] and not os.path.isfile(
586	        os.path.join(member_dir, _FINAL)
587	    ):
588	        # The final was consumed by a staging that got rolled back; the
589	        # member re-assembles from its checkpoints (still no rescan).
590	        return None
591	    try:
592	        src = open(path, "rb")
593	    except OSError:
594	        return None
595	    lineno = int(info["lineno"])
596	    return _LinkedMember(
597	        index, group_index, path, member_dir, src, bool(info["dirty"]),
598	        int(info["offset"]), lineno, 0, 0, lineno,
599	    )
